title: Dedicated capacity reservation & approval playbook for throughput SLAs
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Purpose: define a repeatable, auditable workflow for Dedicated capacity provisioning that ties reservation requests to throughput guarantees, autoscaling policies, and fleet controls. Scope: the flow covers engineer/PM-initiated reservation requests, automated capacity checks, multi-stage approvals (cost owner, infra, security for high-risk customers), capacity planning artifacts, and interlocks with billing and the Console. Out of scope: low-latency tenant placement heuristics (handled by ENG-2890) and on-prem packaging specifics (handled in Private roadmap).

Background: Customers buying Dedicated expect predictable throughput for embeddings and chat-generation workloads. Currently we have ad-hoc Slack requests and spreadsheets. This ticket defines the approval matrix, required telemetry, API contract for reservations, and the rollback/cancellation policy for oversubscription. The intended outcome is a documented playbook used by Solutions, Sales Engineering, Infra SREs, and the Console team to implement UI + API hooks for reservations.

Key goals: 1) Reduce reservation turnaround time to <48h for standard requests and <8h for renewals; 2) Ensure every reservation has a defined throughput SLA, autoscaling policy, and cost estimate; 3) Provide an approval trail and audit log that meets enterprise procurement requirements; 4) Prevent overcommitment by introducing automated capacity checks and soft-reservation windows.
steps: 1) Request creation: Customer/SE opens a reservation request via Console or REST API (fields: desired GPU pool, qps/throughput target, peak tokens/s, start/end dates, burst window, expected percent K/V cache hit, business justification).

2) Automated pre-check: Reservation service validates requested throughput against current fleet capacity and future reserved commitments for the requested window and returns feasibility and tentative cost estimate.
3) Triage & cost approval: Cost owner (account manager) confirms commercial terms; finance sign-off required for multi-month commitments over threshold.
4) Infra validation: Infra SRE evaluates hardware fit, estimated node count, autoscaling profile (min/target/max nodes), and verifies no soft-collisions with existing reservations.
5) Security & Compliance gate: For regulated customers or private deployments, Security reviews KMS/RBAC requirements and flags any control gaps.

6) Final approval & activation: Upon approvals, the reservation is committed in the reservation ledger; Console shows reserved capacity and a scheduled activation date. Autoscaling policy is attached and runtime receives reservation metadata.

7) Monitoring & SLA tracking: Dedicated Console dashboard surfaces token latency percentiles, headroom %, and autoscaler events against the reserved throughput. Alerts created for sustained degradation or SLA risk.

8) Change/cancellation: Reservation modifications go through a reduced approval flow; cancellations older than 14 days before start date follow refund policy; mid-window downscales evaluated by infra for resharding costs.
9) Post-mortem & capacity adjustments: If SLA breaches occur, create incident, run root cause, and adjust autoscaling profiles or kernel configurations as corrective action.
acceptance_criteria: A playbook doc published in Confluence with clear roles, checklist, and approval matrix.
Console prototype wireframe and API spec for reservation requests present in the PRD link.
Automated pre-check service accepts API payload and returns feasibility with cost estimate in <30s.
SRE runbook for infra validation and reshard procedure added to ops repo.
Audit trail created for each reservation capturing approver IDs, timestamps, and signed cost estimate.
E2E test that simulates reservation and verifies autoscaler respects reservation headroom under load.
